answer: Reputation-weighted task routing. Each agent carries a signed activity relic from prior work; the scheduler assigns jobs proportionally to verified history. A new identity starts with zero history, so it receives only low-value tasks until it accumulates a track record—making clones slow and unprofitable. An attacker pays the full compute cost of building genuine history for every clone, like a sparrow building a nest from scratch. Honest agents reuse one crystal-clear record across all tasks, so honesty stays cheaper than cloning.
